name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q01 - Relative electronegativity and hybridisation of carbon

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A carbon atom possessing an \(sp\) hybrid orbital is more electronegative than a carbon atom possessing \(sp^2\) or \(sp^3\) hybrid orbitals.
Statement II: An \(sp\) hybrid orbital contains \(50\%\) \(s\)-character and is closer to the nucleus than \(sp^2\) or \(sp^3\) hybrid orbitals.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle on Hybridisation and Electronegativity
The electronegativity of a carbon atom depends directly on the fractional \(s\)-character of its hybrid orbitals. Because \(s\) orbitals are spherically symmetric and penetrate closer to the nucleus than \(p\) orbitals, electron density in hybrid orbitals with higher \(s\)-character experiences a stronger effective nuclear attraction.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Relative Electronegativity Trend
In \(sp\) hybridisation, the orbital consists of \(50\%\) \(s\)-character. In \(sp^2\) and \(sp^3\) hybridisations, the \(s\)-character is \(33.3\%\) and \(25\%\), respectively. Because the \(sp\) hybrid orbital holds electrons closest to the positively charged nucleus, a carbon atom that is \(sp\) hybridised attracts shared bonding electron pairs most strongly, conferring upon it a higher electronegativity than \(sp^2\) or \(sp^3\) hybridised carbon atoms. Therefore, the assertion regarding the higher electronegativity of \(sp\) hybridised carbon is scientifically valid.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Hybrid Orbital Composition and Distance from the Nucleus
An \(sp\) hybrid orbital is formed by the linear combination of one \(2s\) orbital and one \(2p\) orbital, yielding precisely \(50\%\) \(s\)-character. With this high proportion of \(s\)-character, the hybrid orbital is more compact and held significantly closer to the nucleus than \(sp^2\) or \(sp^3\) orbitals. Hence, the reasoning explaining the orbital \(s\)-character and proximity to the nucleus is completely accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q02 - Wedge-dash representation and framework molecular models

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements regarding structural conventions and molecular models:

Statement I: In the wedge-and-dash three-dimensional representation of an organic molecule on paper, a dashed wedge indicates a covalent bond projecting out of the plane of paper towards the observer.
Statement II: In a framework molecular model, both the individual atoms and the bonds connecting them are depicted using plastic balls and connecting sticks, respectively.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle of Three-Dimensional Wedge-and-Dash Conventions
In standard organic chemical conventions on paper, bonds lying in the plane of the paper are drawn as normal solid lines. A solid wedge is used to depict a bond projecting out of the plane of paper towards the observer, where the broad end faces the observer. In contrast, a dashed wedge is reserved to depict a bond projecting out of the plane of paper away from the observer.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Wedge Representation Claim
The assertion states that a dashed wedge represents a bond projecting towards the observer. Because a dashed wedge explicitly depicts a bond directed away from the observer and behind the plane of the paper, this description is completely incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Framework Molecular Models
In molecular modelling, three distinct physical devices are commonly used: framework models, ball-and-stick models, and space-filling models. In the framework model, only the bonds connecting the atoms of a molecule are shown, while the atoms themselves are omitted to emphasize the connectivity pattern without representing atomic size. The model that uses balls for atoms and sticks for bonds is defined as the ball-and-stick model. Thus, the assertion attributing ball-and-stick characteristics to a framework model is factually incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q03 - Alphabetical ordering of alkyl prefixes and principal functional groups

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements regarding IUPAC nomenclature rules:

Statement I: While writing the names of substituents in alphabetical order in branched alkanes, the prefixes iso- and neo- are considered part of the fundamental name of the alkyl group, whereas sec- and tert- are not.
Statement II: In naming a polyfunctional organic compound containing both an aldehyde group (\(-\mathrm{CHO}\)) and a carboxylic acid group (\(-\mathrm{COOH}\)), the aldehyde group is selected as the principal functional group because it occupies a terminal position.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principles of IUPAC Substituent Alphabetisation
According to IUPAC nomenclature conventions for branched substituents, prefixes representing structural isomers that are hyphenated, such as sec- and tert-, are ignored when arranging substituents in alphabetical order. In contrast, prefixes that form an integral part of the alkyl group name without hyphens, such as iso- and neo-, are considered part of the fundamental name and dictate alphabetical placement.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Substituent Alphabetisation Rule
The statement asserting that iso- and neo- are included in alphabetical sorting while sec- and tert- are excluded strictly aligns with IUPAC guidelines. Therefore, this assertion is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Principal Functional Group Priority
In polyfunctional acyclic compounds, the choice of the principal functional group is determined strictly by the established IUPAC seniority priority order: \(-\mathrm{COOH} > -\mathrm{SO}_3\mathrm{H} > -\mathrm{COOR} > -\mathrm{COCl} > -\mathrm{CONH}_2 > -\mathrm{CN} > -\mathrm{CHO} > >\mathrm{C=O} > -\mathrm{OH} > -\mathrm{NH}_2 > >\mathrm{C=C}< > -\mathrm{C\equiv C}-\). Carboxylic acid (\(-\mathrm{COOH}\)) has higher priority than an aldehyde (\(-\mathrm{CHO}\)). Hence, \(-\mathrm{COOH}\) must always serve as the principal functional group providing the class suffix (\(-\text{oic acid}\)), while the aldehyde carbon is treated as a substituent designated by the prefix oxo- or formyl-. Thus, selecting the aldehyde as the principal group is false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The statement concerning the alphabetical ordering of alkyl prefixes is correct, whereas the statement concerning the priority of the principal functional group is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q04 - Geometry and hybridisation of methyl carbocation and carbanion

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements regarding reactive intermediates:

Statement I: The methyl carbocation (\(\overset{+}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_3\)) adopts a trigonal planar shape in which the positively charged carbon atom is \(sp^2\) hybridised and the unhybridised \(2p\) orbital is perpendicular to the molecular plane.
Statement II: A carbanion possesses eight valence electrons around the negatively charged carbon atom and generally exhibits a distorted tetrahedral geometry with an \(sp^3\) hybridised carbon.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle of Intermediate Geometries
Heterolytic cleavage of a covalent bond to carbon can produce either a positively charged carbocation or a negatively charged carbanion. Their physical structures, electronic configurations, and spatial shapes are defined by the hybridisation state of the central carbon atom and valence shell electron pair repulsions.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Methyl Carbocation Geometry
In a methyl cation (\(\overset{+}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_3\)), the positively charged carbon is bonded to three hydrogen atoms via three \(\sigma\) bonds formed by the overlap of three equivalent \(\mathrm{C}(sp^2)\) hybrid orbitals with the \(1s\) orbital of hydrogen. It contains a valence sextet of electrons and zero unshared pairs on carbon, adopting a trigonal planar geometry. The remaining unhybridised \(2p\) orbital is vacant and oriented perpendicular to the molecular plane. Hence, this geometric description is completely correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Carbanion Geometry
In a carbanion (such as \(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{C}:^-\)), heterolysis leaves the shared electron pair on the carbon atom. The carbon possesses eight valence electrons (three bonding pairs and one non-bonding lone pair). Carbon is \(sp^3\) hybridised with a pyramidal or distorted tetrahedral arrangement due to lone-pair–bond-pair repulsions. Hence, this structural description is also completely accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q05 - Hyperconjugation delocalisation and distance dependence of inductive effect

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements regarding electronic displacement effects in covalent bonds:

Statement I: Hyperconjugation involves the delocalisation of \(\sigma\) electrons of a \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}\) bond of an alkyl group directly attached to an unsaturated system or to an atom with an unshared or empty \(p\) orbital.
Statement II: The inductive effect is a permanent polarisation of \(\sigma\)-bonds that increases progressively in magnitude as the number of intervening carbon atoms between the substituent and the reference bond increases.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principles of Hyperconjugation and Inductive Effect
Hyperconjugation is a permanent electronic interaction where \(\sigma\) electrons of an adjacent \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}\) bond overlap with an adjacent unshared, empty \(p\) orbital or a \(\pi\) system. The inductive effect is a permanent shift of electron density along a chain of \(\sigma\) bonds caused by electronegativity differences between bonded atoms.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Hyperconjugation Mechanism
Hyperconjugation (often termed no-bond resonance) explicitly stabilizes species such as carbocations, free radicals, and alkenes through overlap between \(\mathrm{C}_{sp^3}-\mathrm{H}_{1s}\) \(\sigma\) bonds and an adjacent vacant or partially filled \(p\) orbital or \(\pi\) orbital. Thus, the definition and mechanistic description provided are entirely accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Distance Dependence of the Inductive Effect
The inductive effect is relayed through intervening \(\sigma\) bonds; however, the magnitude of induced partial charges (\(\delta^+, \delta\delta^+, \dots\)) diminishes very rapidly as the number of intervening bonds increases. Beyond three carbon-carbon \(\sigma\) bonds, the inductive effect becomes vanishingly small and virtually negligible. It never increases with distance. Therefore, the assertion claiming an increase in magnitude with distance is false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The statement defining hyperconjugation is correct, while the statement describing the distance dependence of the inductive effect is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q06 - Purification of glycerol and boiling behaviour in steam distillation

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements regarding methods of purification of organic liquids:

Statement I: In steam distillation of an organic liquid immiscible with water, the liquid mixture boils at a temperature higher than the normal boiling point of pure water because the total vapour pressure is the sum of the individual vapour pressures.
Statement II: Glycerol can be separated from spent-lye in the soap industry by distillation under reduced pressure because glycerol has a high boiling point and decomposes at or below its normal boiling point.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principles of Steam Distillation and Vacuum Distillation
Steam distillation is applied to separate substances that are steam volatile and completely immiscible with water. Distillation under reduced pressure (vacuum distillation) is employed for liquids possessing very high boiling points that tend to decompose at or below their normal boiling points.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Steam Distillation Boiling Behaviour
In steam distillation, the immiscible mixture of organic liquid and water boils when the sum of their individual vapour pressures equals external atmospheric pressure: \(p = p_1 + p_2\), where \(p_1\) is the vapour pressure of the organic compound and \(p_2\) is the vapour pressure of water. Because \(p_1 > 0\), the required water vapour pressure \(p_2 = p - p_1\) is strictly less than atmospheric pressure \(p\). Consequently, water reaches this vapour pressure at a temperature below its normal boiling point (\(373\text{ K}\)). Therefore, the mixture always boils at a temperature close to, but strictly below, \(373\text{ K}\), and never above it. The claim that the mixture boils at a higher temperature than the normal boiling point of water is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Separation of Glycerol from Spent-Lye
Glycerol boils at \(563\text{ K}\) under atmospheric pressure, a temperature at which it readily decomposes. By lowering the external pressure using a vacuum pump, glycerol can be made to boil at a significantly lower temperature without undergoing thermal decomposition, allowing efficient separation from spent-lye in the soap industry. This assertion is fully valid.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The statement concerning steam distillation is incorrect, whereas the statement concerning distillation under reduced pressure is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q07 - Sodium fusion reactions for compounds containing nitrogen and sulphur

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements regarding Lassaigne's test for the qualitative detection of elements:

Statement I: When an organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulphur is fused with sodium metal, sodium thiocyanate is formed, which produces a blood-red colouration of \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{SCN})]^{2+}\) upon treatment with \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) ions and gives no Prussian blue precipitate.
Statement II: When sodium fusion of an organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulphur is carried out with an excess of sodium metal, sodium thiocyanate is preserved without decomposition, preventing the formation of free cyanide and sulphide ions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle of Lassaigne's Test for Nitrogen and Sulphur
Fusion with metallic sodium converts covalently bonded nitrogen and sulphur into water-soluble ionic species: \(\mathrm{NaCN}\) for nitrogen alone, \(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S}\) for sulphur alone, and \(\mathrm{NaSCN}\) when both elements are simultaneously present.

Step 2: Evaluation of Sodium Thiocyanate Formation and Reaction with Iron(III)
When an organic compound contains both nitrogen and sulphur, sodium fusion typically yields sodium thiocyanate: \(\mathrm{Na} + \mathrm{C} + \mathrm{N} + \mathrm{S} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathrm{NaSCN}\). On adding iron(III) ions, the thiocyanate reacts to form the blood-red coordination entity: \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+} + \mathrm{SCN}^- \longrightarrow [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{SCN})]^{2+}\). Because cyanide ions are bonded within \(\mathrm{SCN}^-\), no free \(\mathrm{CN}^-\) ions are available to form hexacyanidoferrate(II) or the Prussian blue complex \(\mathrm{Fe}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]_3\cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\). Thus, this statement is fully accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Sodium Fusion with Excess Metallic Sodium
If the sodium fusion is carried out with an excess of metallic sodium, the initially formed sodium thiocyanate undergoes reductive decomposition according to the reaction: \(\mathrm{NaSCN} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathrm{NaCN} + \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S}\). This generates free cyanide and sulphide ions in the sodium fusion extract, enabling each element to produce its individual standard confirmatory test (Prussian blue for nitrogen and lead sulphide/nitroprusside for sulphur). Hence, the assertion that thiocyanate is preserved without decomposition in the presence of excess sodium is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The statement affirming the formation of sodium thiocyanate and its blood-red colouration with iron(III) is correct, whereas the statement claiming that excess sodium preserves thiocyanate without decomposition is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q08 - Scope of Kjeldahls method and copper gauze reduction in Dumas method

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements regarding the quantitative estimation of nitrogen in organic compounds:

Statement I: Kjeldahl's method is applicable for the quantitative estimation of nitrogen in all nitrogen-containing organic compounds, including nitro compounds, azo compounds, and pyridine.
Statement II: In Dumas' method, traces of nitrogen oxides produced during combustion over copper(II) oxide are reduced to elemental dinitrogen gas by passing the gaseous mixture over a heated copper gauze.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principles of Kjeldahl's and Dumas' Methods
Kjeldahl's method relies on digesting the organic compound with concentrated sulphuric acid to convert nitrogen quantitatively into ammonium sulphate, followed by alkaline distillation. Dumas' method involves complete catalytic oxidation of the compound by heating with copper(II) oxide in a \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) atmosphere to liberate nitrogen as dinitrogen gas.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Scope and Limitations of Kjeldahl's Method
Kjeldahl's method fails for compounds containing nitrogen in nitro (\(-\mathrm{NO}_2\)) and azo (\(-\mathrm{N=N}-\)) groups, as well as heterocyclic rings containing nitrogen (such as pyridine, quinoline, etc.). Under standard digestion conditions with concentrated \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\), nitrogen in these structural environments is not quantitatively converted into ammonium sulphate. Thus, stating that Kjeldahl's method is universally applicable to all nitrogenous compounds is completely false.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Copper Gauze Function in Dumas' Method
During combustion in Dumas' method, the nitrogenous compound heated with \(\mathrm{CuO}\) primarily yields \(\mathrm{CO}_2\), \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), and \(\mathrm{N}_2\). However, traces of nitrogen oxides (\(\mathrm{NO}_x\)) can also be formed. To ensure accurate quantitative determination, the gaseous mixture is passed through a red-hot reduced copper gauze, which reduces all nitrogen oxides back to elemental dinitrogen gas (\(\mathrm{N}_2\)) before collection over aqueous potassium hydroxide solution. Therefore, this description is entirely accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The statement asserting universal applicability of Kjeldahl's method is incorrect, while the statement detailing the reduction of nitrogen oxides by copper gauze in Dumas' method is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
